title: A laser-mediated photo-manipulative toolbox for generation and real-time monitoring of DNA lesions
protocol: Seed cells in the chambered slide in phenol red-free DMEM medium.
Incubate seeded cells under normal cell growth conditions at 37°C, 5% CO2, and 90%-95% relative humidity (RH).
Replace the culture medium from each well with fresh DMEM medium (250 μL/well) on DAY-2.
Select the proper positive control plasmid for DSB repair.
Choose a fluorescent-tagged early DNA damage sensing factor such as Nbs1 or nuclear sirtuins.
Plan to use Nbs1 if studying late stages of repair due to its long presence at the damage site.
Consider using SIRT1, SIRT6, or SIRT7 for recruitment within 20 seconds after damage.
Select a second plasmid based on experimental objectives and cell pathway usage.
Choose markers from pathways (i) BLM-DNA2-RPA-MRN or (ii) EXO1-BLM-RPA-MRN.
Prepare the transfection mix as per table conditions for Hela, U2OS and A549 cells using Turbofect transfection reagent.
Replace the culture medium six hours post-transfection with phenol red-free complete DMEM supplemented with 10 μM BrdU in each well.
Incubate the cells in a cell culture incubator for 24 h.
Turn on the microscope incubator and set temperature to 37°C, CO2 to 5%, and relative humidity to 90%–95%.
Transfer chambered slide containing transfected cells onto the pre-warmed incubator-microscope stage.
Locate, focus, and zoom-in over transfected cells (zoom factor 3-3.2×).
Check for intact nuclear morphology and uniform fluorescence in the nucleus.
Decide the region of interest (ROI) shape for laser irradiation.
Choose a single straight line across the nucleus as the ROI shape.
Draw the straight line across the nucleus to be irradiated by laser.
Set the time interval and total duration for live microscopy.
Adjust conditions for time-lapse imaging according to the dynamics of the sub-process studied.
Use a time interval of 5-10 seconds post DNA damage when studying factors such as SIRT6, SIRT1, vRAGE after Nbs1 recruitment.
Track recruitment kinetics over an interval as low as 0.5 seconds if using FV1000/FV1200.
Depend the total duration of live-cell microscopy on the repair factor and process to be studied.
Start tracking DNA damage sensor complex related factors from 1 to 120 seconds after laser-induced DNA damage.
Monitor MRN (MRE11-RAD50-Nbs1) complex recruitment until it reaches maximum saturation intensity within 10-90 seconds.
Track resection events from 2-5 minutes for short-range resection or longer for long-range resection.
Start the acquisition to track changes.
Induce minor photo-bleaching across a selected shape using laser irradiation.
Monitor recovery of SIRT7-EGFP fluorescence within seconds after bleaching.
Record representative time-points for the recruitment of EGFP-SIRT7 and vRAGE-mCherry at the site of DNA DSBs in BrdU pre-sensitized U2OS cells.
Quantify the fluorescence intensity of EGFP-SIRT7 and mCherry-vRAGE before and after laser-induced DNA damage.
Plot the relative fluorescence intensity at each time point, indicating SEM values for irradiated versus unirradiated regions (n > 3).
Monitor recruitment kinetics of the study factor (mCherry-vRAGE) at the site of irradiation.
Save the recorded video.
Process the data using ImageJ or comparable software.
Open the recorded videos in ImageJ.
Select and draw a straight line on the damaged area using ROI manager.
Measure fluorescence intensity values for all slices from the “more” window of ROI manager.
Copy the result values into an excel file.
Repeat measurements in the undamaged area for all time points/slices.
Calculate mean fluorescence intensity of irradiated region (ROIirr) divided by fluorescence intensity of unirradiated (ROIunirr).
Normalize final values with the fluorescence intensity at pre-damage (t=0) of the experiment.
Plot normalized values against the time interval used during video microscopy.
Seed cells in respective wells of the chambered slide in complete phenol red-free DMEM medium supplemented with 10 μM BrdU.
Incubate seeded cells under normal cell growth conditions.
Set the microscope incubator temperature to 37°C.
Set the CO2 level to 5%.
Set the relative humidity to 90%-95%.
Turn on the microscope and laser boxes.
Start the software and load the settings/parameters described in DSBs Protocol (step-f).
Let the environment chamber warm up for at least an hour.
Transfer slide containing cells (Grid-500) onto the pre-warmed incubator-microscope stage after 24 h of BrdU pre-sensitization.
Focus and locate well-grown areas of cells in the culture well.
Find a region where cells are well spaced and healthy.
Note down lane markings on the surface grid.
Draw a line across the cell nucleus to damage it.
Target either a single cell or multiple cells at a time.
Use laser settings described in DSBs Protocol (step-i).
Activate the damage pulse for 250 ms.
Repeat steps quickly to irradiate the desired number of cells in the same or other wells.
Remove the cell culture medium from the irradiated well.
Wash the growth surface three times with 1× PBS.
Fix the cells using ice-cold PFA at a volume of 250 μL per well.
Incubate fixed cells at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Remove Paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Incubate fixed cells once with 50 mM Tris-Cl (pH=7.5) to inactivate residual PFA.
Wash the fixed cells twice with 1× PBS, each for 5 minutes.
Pre-extract irradiated cells in CSK buffer before fixation if the expression of the factor is low or recruitment weak.
Treat live cells with CSK buffer partially permeabilizing them and releasing unbound cytosolic/nucleoplasmic contents without affecting factors bound to sub-cellular structures and chromatin.
Determine the time of CSK extraction empirically based on cell types used in the study.
Use Triton X-100 concentration and time successfully applied for fibroblasts (0.1%, 1–2 min), U2OS (0.2%, 3 min), Hela, and A549 (0.3%, 4 min).
Proceed with immunofluorescence (IF) staining protocol.
Locate the irradiated cells as noted in step-q.
Image the irradiated cells.
Seed cells in the chambered slide in complete phenol red-free DMEM medium.
Incubate seeded cells under normal cell growth conditions at 37°C, 5% CO2, and 90%-95% relative humidity (RH).
Replace the culture medium from each well with fresh DMEM medium after incubation for about 16-24 hours.
Transfect cells with control plasmid and desired study plasmid as per experimental plan.
Incubate transfected cells with fresh phenol red-free DMEM for 24–36 hours in a cell culture incubator.
Turn on the microscope incubator.
Set the incubator temperature to 37°C.
Set the CO2 level in the incubator to 5%.
Set the relative humidity in the incubator to 90%-95%.
Turn on the microscope.
Start the microscope program software and load settings/parameters.
Prepare cells for ICL damage by pre-sensitizing them with 25 μM of TM-Psoralen for 15 minutes.
Discard any leftover TMP solution older than 12 hours as per disposal guidelines.
Transfer chambered slide with sensitized/transfected cells onto the microscope stage.
Select suitable cells expressing EGFP and mCherry or other fluorescent tags.
Fine focus and zoom-in to the respective well to locate an extended, well-grown cell with intact nuclear morphology and uniform fluorescence in the nucleus.
Select the 355 nm laser in the SIM settings window.
Load/write parameters for other settings as described in DSBs Protocol (step-i).
Set an exposure time of 300–400 ms for ICL factors.
Decide the shape and nuclear area to expose to radiation.
Draw the ROI as described in DSBs Protocol (step-j).
Set the region to irradiate.
Set a time interval and total duration, starting with intervals of 15–20 s.
Start the time-lapse recording.
Track the recruitment kinetics of the ICL repair positive control and test factor.
Use EGFP-tagged human FANCD2 for this assay.
Use mCherry-tagged human vRAGE for this assay.
Save the recorded video.
Arrange the data as presented in DSBs Protocol (step-m).
Quantify the fluorescence intensity of EGFP-FANCD2 and mCherry-vRAGE before and after laser-induced DNA damage.
Plot the relative fluorescence intensity of indicated factors in irradiated versus unirradiated regions.
Seed cells in phenol red-free complete DMEM medium in chambered slides or Cellview culture dishes in the evening.
Incubate cells overnight to allow attachment and growth.
Fix cells with Paraformaldehyde (PFA) based fixation solution.
Stain cells using immunofluorescence (IF) staining method with appropriate antibodies.
Capture images of stained cells to analyze fluorescence intensity.
Turn on the microscope incubator.
Set the incubator temperature to 37°C.
Set the CO2 level to 5%.
Set the relative humidity to 90–95%.
Turn on the microscope and laser boxes.
Open the software and load the settings/parameters described in the instrumental setup.
Pre-sensitize growing cells with 25 μM of TM-Psoralen for 30 minutes.
Focus into the culture well using zoom factor 3–3.2×.
Locate a region where cells are well spaced and healthy.
Note down the lane markings in the surface grid.
Select the 355 nm laser in the settings.
Load/write parameters as described for ICL live microscopy.
Decide the shape and nuclear area to expose to radiation.
Draw the ROI accordingly.
Laser irradiates the cell as described in live-cell experiment ICLs Protocol.
Repeat steps from ICLs Protocol (step-q to t) for inducing the desired number of cells in the same or other wells quickly.
Determine post-irradiation time as 5, 10, 15, 30, or 60 minutes based on the experiment's objective.
Process irradiated cells as described earlier for DSBs in Protocol (step-u to v).
Fix cells in 15 minutes if studying ICLs sensor signaling/recruitment like SLX4.
Wait at least 30–45 minutes before fixation if studying nuclease-mediated unhooking of ICLs.
Stain processed cells with respective antibodies.
Locate irradiated cells using the noted grid coordinates from ICLs Protocol (step-p).
Refer to DSBs Protocol (step-v) for immunofluorescence staining guide details.
Inspect and process data with ImageJ or similar software.
Seed cells in phenol red-free complete DMEM medium in the chambered slide.
Replace the culture medium from each well with fresh DMEM medium.
Prepare the transfection mix with the study plasmids as shown in Tables 1 and 3.
Replace the medium with phenol red-free DMEM about 6 hours post-transfection.
Incubate the cells for 24 h.
Turn on the microscope incubator.
Set the microscope incubator temperature to 37°C, CO2 level to 5%, and relative humidity to 90%–95%.
Transfer the chambered slide containing transfected cells onto the microscope stage after 24 hours of post-transfection.
Visualize the EGFP and other fluorescence mCherry in the cells.
Focus on a well-extended cell with intact nuclear morphology and uniform fluorescence in the nucleus.
Select the 355 nm Laser in the settings window.
Set the exposure time to 100–150 ms.
Draw the region of interest (ROI) as needed.
Set the time interval and total duration for live microscopy.
Begin observing DNA damage response/recruitment kinetics after every 15–20 seconds.
Start the time-lapse to track recruitment kinetics.
Adapt time and total duration settings if necessary.
Track single-strand break repair positive control and test factor.
Use mCherry tagged human PARP1 for tracking.
Use EGFP-tagged human Cockayne syndrome group B (Csb) for tracking.
Save recorded time-lapse data.
Process the data using ImageJ or similar software.
Seed cells in Phenol red-free complete DMEM medium in the chambered slide.
Set the microscope incubator temperature to 37°C and RH to 90%–95%.
Transfer chambered grid slide containing cells onto the microscope stage.
Focus on the well extended/grown cell with intact nuclear morphology.
Select 355 nm Laser in settings window.
Load/write parameters for live microscopy SSBs Protocol.
Decide shape and nuclear area to expose to radiation.
Draw ROI as needed according to DSBs Protocol.
Use laser settings described in ssDNA damage live microscopy protocol.
Irradiate nuclei accordingly.
Work quickly and repeat steps as required.
Process irradiated cells after suitable post-irradiation time as per Table 4 description for ss-DNA damage.
Proceed to IF staining with study markers according to DSBs Protocol.
